drivers.title: Near-certain US rate hike in December
drivers.detail: Kitco reports roughly 90% odds of a 25 bp Fed hike in December; Fed Governor Waller has floated a 50 bp move. Higher rates make non-yielding metals less attractive.

drivers.title: Hawkish Fed minutes
drivers.detail: Minutes of the October meeting showed policymakers saw rising inflation risks that may need a stronger response; markets fully price a December hike.

drivers.title: Strong dollar, 10-year yield above 5%
drivers.detail: The dollar index this week hit its highest since April 2025, making gold costlier for non-US buyers; the 10-year Treasury yield is just above 5%.

drivers.title: ETF outflows and slower central-bank buying
drivers.detail: World Gold Council data show November ETF outflows turned year-to-date ETF demand negative; Poland likely paused buying after reaching its 700-tonne target. Gold is also being sold to raise cash.

drivers.title: Weaker silver demand forecast
drivers.detail: Metals Focus research for the Silver Institute forecasts a 5% fall in global silver demand in 2026 on weaker jewellery and solar-cell use.

drivers.title: Rupee strengthens for 4th session
drivers.detail: The rupee closed at 93.32 per dollar on FII inflows and strong equities. A stronger rupee lowers the rupee price of imported gold and silver.

drivers.title: Safe-haven demand not helping
drivers.detail: Softer US data, a 2% fall in the S&P 500 and Strait of Hormuz tensions did not lift gold, which signals that selling pressure is dominant for now.

events.title: US November CPI (inflation) report
events.why: Seen as the next major catalyst for gold before the Fed decision.

events.title: Fed December policy meeting
events.why: A rate hike is largely priced in; a 50 bp hike or hawkish guidance would add pressure, a pause would likely lift metals.

views.view: Sees downside as more likely; target $3,500 gold and $40 silver; resistance $3,837–3,870.
Called the small rebound more likely profit-taking by bears than a real catalyst.

highlights.text: Gold fell below $3,550 this morning, down about 8.9% this week (its worst week since March); silver is below $42.
Main reason: markets are pricing in about a 90% chance of a US rate hike in December, and the dollar is at a 19-month high.
Indian rates are falling sharply today: MCX gold futures are down nearly 4% at ₹1,22,430 per 10 g; SY expects today's IBJA 24K near ₹12,350/g.
Next big event: the US inflation (CPI) report on 10 Dec, ahead of the Fed's December decision. Expect large moves around those dates.

guidance.summary: Prices are in a clear downtrend, and daily moves of 2–3% are common right now. Nobody can reliably call the bottom. If you need gold or silver, how you buy matters more than the exact day you buy.

points.who: Buying jewellery for a fixed date (wedding, festival)
points.tip: Don't wait for the bottom. Spread the purchase over 2–4 weeks, or use a jeweller's rate-booking or advance scheme so a sudden rebound doesn't hurt you.

Buy in small fixed amounts each week or month instead of one lump sum, especially before the 10 Dec US CPI report and the Fed decision. Gold has grown about 15% a year in rupees over 10 years, but it fell about 26% from its Feb 2026 peak, so think in years, not days.
Selling in panic after a big fall locks in the loss. Check whether your reason for holding (long-term saving, hedge against a weak rupee) still applies.
Silver moves about 1.5× as much as gold, both up and down. Keep it a smaller share than gold unless you can handle big swings.
Compare the jeweller's per-gram rate with today's IBJA rate in this app. Add 3% GST and making charges, which vary widely, so ask for them separately. Insist on the BIS hallmark with a HUID number.
